newsitem.title: UK: Investors celebrate Russia's long-awaited return.
newsitem.headline: Investors celebrate Russia's long-awaited return.

text.p: Russia's $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond launch on Thursday was deemed a success both by bankers involved in the issue and at rival firms.
"There's a celebration from people who have an appetite to take some risk, who can finally find better than seven percent returns out of Europe," an Eastern European economist said.
Russia raised double the expected amount of money at well below the anticipated cost, recording a red-letter day for the country after an 80-year absence from international markets.
The Eurobond was priced to yield 345 basis points (bp) more than five-year U.S. Treasury notes via joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg.
The Eurobond pays a 9.25 percent coupon which was helped by the recent rally in the U.S. Treasury market, traders said.

A number of hurdles had to be cleared before the launch. These included the Russian presidential elections mid-year, credit ratings from the key rating agencies and, latterly, president Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery.

"There were times people thought Russia would launch at 600-700 basis points over. The Russians were never worried about this, but it gives a feel for how broad a transformation there has been in investor sentiment," an analyst said.
It was the country's first international bond offering since the 1917 revolution.
"It's been outstanding, I'm very pleased that Russia has been able to re-enter the international bond markets in such a dramatic way," a syndicate official said.

Kleinwort Benson emerging markets economist Anthony Thomas told Reuters Financial Television "Russia has done a very good job of stabilising their economy. They have brought the inflation rate down, stabilised the currency and made a lot of progress in reducing the budget deficit."

Bankers said demand was in excess of $2.0 billion in orders. "I know there were substantial number of investors who said 350 b.p. was the minimum for the deal, so tightening it to 345 b.p. was an exercise in capping the demand," one bankers said.
The launch followed a promotional extravaganza in which three teams of Russian officials and bankers spanned 14 cities in two weeks, kicking off in Tokyo and culminating in New York.
Investors and bankers flocked to a presentation in London last Friday where Russia's finance minister Alexander Livshits said he wanted the Eurobond to show the country was a respectable borrower.
"I'm very pleased for the Russians. I think people have not appreciated how difficult and painful the economic adjustment has been," an emerging market anaylst at a U.S. bank said.
Another said "Russia is getting its proper reward for years of hard effort in restructuring its debt."
The Eurobond will pave the way for other Russian borrowers to follow, such as the cities of Moscow, St Petersburg and the Sverdlovsk region.
"It opens up a new market and next year, we'll see Russia tap other currencies and set a yield curve for other Russian corporates, agencies and utilities to follow," a dealer said.
Companies like Russia's RAO Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer, Russia's biggest oil group NK LUKoil LKOH.RTS and the Russian Railways Ministry are likely to follow suit.

Russia was rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB minus by Standard & Poor's, which are below investment grade but were at the top end of market expectations when assigned in October. Today, IBCA affirmed its BB plus rating for Russia.

In the draft of the Russian budget for next year submitted in September, Russia has set a target of $1.3 billion of borrowing in the international capital markets. Analysts said this figure could be revised given the success of today's deal.
